content: Rumenic acid is a specific type of conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) that is predominantly found in the fat of ruminant animals and in dairy products derived from them. It is classified as an omega-7 trans fat. The chemical shorthand for this fatty acid is cis-9, trans-11 18:2 acid. The term rumenic acid was first introduced by Kramer and colleagues in 1998. This fatty acid is produced in the rumen of ruminant animals through a process called biohydrogenation, during which dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids are metabolized. Alongside vaccenic acid, rumenic acid is one of the key products of this metabolic process. It represents the primary dietary form of CLA, accounting for approximately 85-90% of the total CLA content found in dairy products. Laboratory research has demonstrated that rumenic acid exhibits anticancer properties, suggesting its potential role in cancer prevention or therapy.
